newsitem.title: USA: January new-home sales highest in nearly 11 years.
newsitem.headline: January new-home sales highest in nearly 11 years.

text.p: Sales of new homes shot upward unexpectedly in January to the highest level in nearly 11 years, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday.
Sales increased 8.6 percent in January to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 870,000 units -- the highest rate since 880,000 in March 1986 -- after a revised 0.5 percent rise in December.
The department said it was starting to use a new, computerized method to collect information on new-home sales and said there might be some "upward bias" in the numbers initially.
Commerce said more than half the January sales data were collected using the computerized system. It said that "during this transition period there seems to be some upward bias in the estimates."
The department said it was using procedures to "dampen monthly fluctuations" in the sales estimates under the new collection method.
The January sales information was sharply contrary to Wall Street economists' expectations that sales would drop to a rate of 757,000 a year instead of soar upward.
January sales were 19.7 percent higher than a year earlier, in January 1996, when new homes were selling at a rate of 727,000 a year.
The sales increase this January was heavily concentrated in the Northeast, where sales jumped 63.4 percent to 134,000 a year -- the highest since 152,000 in November 1987.
The only other region where sales rose during January was the South, where they were up 11.9 percent to 403,000 -- the highest since 440,000 in December 1983.
By contrast, sales fell 10.3 percent from December levels in the Midwest to 140,000 a year during January and in the West they were down 5.9 percent to 192,000.
Previously, the department said December sales had fallen 1 percent to an annual rate of 783,000. But it revised that to show a 0.5 percent gain to a much higher level of 801,000.
The pickup in January sales came despite higher mortgage rates.

The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said rates for a 30-year mortgage averaged 7.82 percent in January, up from 7.6 percent in December. It also was higher than the 7.03 percent mortgage rate available a year earlier in January 1996.
Last week, the National Association of Realtors said sales of existing, or used, homes rose 2.1 percent in January to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.94 million.
The average home sales price in January rose to $172,800 from $171,300 in December while the median sales price was up to $145,000 from $143,000.
